findings.title: Listen names, and counts, a killer veiled for the opening
findings.what_happens: Listen runs on the player's own browser and reads who is in the room through occupantsOf -> othersInNamedRoom -> countsAsPresent, which leaves out only a token with Foundry's `hidden`. Since E112v the veil writes no `hidden` (only the module's flag), so the veiled killer counts. listenName cuts masked names only. The pickers were moved to seenHere for MAP-16; Listen and its Reroll were not.
findings.evidence: action-listen.mjs:237 `const who = occupantsOf(target, actor, scene).map(listenName);` and :120-122 `return isMaskedActor(other) ? MASK_NAME : other?.name ?? "";`; movement.mjs:3868-3869 `// The opening's veil (E112) hides a killer from the other players, not from the room ... return !hiddenByGm(doc);`; utils.mjs:443-446 hiddenByGm reads `doc?.hidden` alone. The audit's own recheck-119 MAP-16 residue says it in one line: "Listen's named tier (action-listen.mjs:120-122) hides masked names only" - not routed to a line.
findings.failure_scenario: Chie opens a direct murder on Aiko in the Library; the opening waits on Chie's roll, Chie veiled. Botan, a bystander in the Hall next door (not seated: allowed-now's action road shuts only a fighter, an Eclipse or a trial), presses Listen on the Library and rolls the named tier: his card says the Library holds Aiko and Chie Mori, while his map draws no Chie and every picker leaves her out. On the pass tier it says two people are there; a critical sweep names her too. The same through a Reroll of that Listen (heardLines on Botan's browser).
findings.refutation_tried: Looked for a veil filter on the way: performListen (action-listen.mjs:155-246) calls no seenHere or veiledFromHere; occupantsOf is othersInNamedRoom (movement.mjs:4154-4156); countsAsPresent keeps a veiled token by its own comment; allowed-now.mjs:60-62 does not shut Listen for an unseated student while the opening waits. Not run on the harness.

verifier.why: Could not overturn. (1) Listen can run while the veil stands: the veil is wanted only at murderState stage 'openingRoll' (mask-gm.mjs:429-431) or as the lights' rows after an Eclipse has ended (mask-gm.mjs:385-387), and no gate shuts Listen then. performAction's fight test is stage === 'incident' && sideOf (action-rolls.mjs:133-134), so at 'openingRoll' nobody is 'fighting'; allowed-now.mjs:60-62 shuts only an Eclipse, a fight and a trial; the sheet tile reads the same facts (sheet-actions.mjs:1255, :1279). A bystander - and the victim too, who is not seated at the opening (settings.mjs:3696) - can press Listen. For an Eclipse murder this is the first moment Listen is open at all after the dark crossing (Listen is shut in the Eclipse), so the veil's wait is exactly when the named tier is most worth having. (2) Who sees the result: the listener alone (and the GMs). performListen posts with whisperToOwner (action-listen.mjs:254; utils.mjs:751-758: gmIds plus the actor's owners, through privately), no public card; the Reroll's lines are built on the roller's own browser (reroll.mjs:1898-1929). The words are cut by secret.mjs wordsFor, whose name cut covers masks only (nameMask, heldMaskNames), and no mask stands during the veil, so the name goes out in clear and stays in the listener's copy after a mask goes on (the card was remembered with no hid). (3) The predicate exists and fits: mask-gm.mjs:736-747 veiledFromHere / seenHere, already used by every picker since 1.2.119 (action-tail.mjs:28, call-pickers.mjs:406, handover.mjs:61, monocub.mjs:910). For a veiled token tokenShownTo answers 'hide' to everyone but the owner and the killers' side (visibility.mjs:555-561), independent of the room rule, so seenHere(occupantsOf(...)) at action-listen.mjs:228, :237 and :245 and reroll.mjs:1916 and :1925 would drop the veiled killer for a bystander and keep them for the killers' side; action-listen.mjs already imports from mask-gm.mjs (:29). No test pins the opposite (no tier-1 or tier-2 body reads Listen with a veiled token). Narrowing, not enough to lower it: not new in 1.2.121 - countsAsPresent has read past the veil since E112 (1.2.116, docs/dev/e112/STATUS.md:59-61; movement.mjs:3868-3869), and recheck-119's MAP-16 residue already named Listen's tier; the named tier needs the action's highest threshold or a critical, the pass tier only gives a count, and the window lasts while the opening (or the lights) waits. Major because it is the owner-115 item 1 rule ('secret for bystanders too') broken on a player's own screen without a console, and it ties the later '?' to a name; the same class (a picker naming the veiled killer) was filed as a blocker in 1.2.119.

findings.title: A room action's reply still names a masked target in clear to the user's browser
findings.what_happens: M1 cut a veiled target's line from both the reply and tellUse's card, but a target behind a mask (after the opening on Hope, until the time of day ends) is cut only on the card, by secret.mjs wordsFor. The reply that goes back over the bridge to the player who used the action carries `target.name` as written. A Reroll of the room action returns the same lines in its reply. The window does not draw the lines (action-rest.mjs:43 returns them), so a player reads them from the console or the packet; D2: a player's browser is trusted with nothing that belongs to somebody else.

findings.title: A second GM never hears a reveal and keeps the revealed killer's name cut on the cards it serves and rewrites
findings.what_happens: forgetHeldMask runs only on the GM that ran endMask(..., 'reveal'). Every other GM's store keeps its `hid` rows, so after the killer reveals themselves that GM's answer to a returning reader and any rewrite it makes (updateSecret sends with the entry's hid) write '?' over a name the table was shown. The line restates this as intended ('the side that hides'); not widened by 1.2.121 (a reveal is only possible while the mask stands, when the second GM's remember already took maskedNow), but now documented as the rule while the release notes say 'until the killer reveals themselves'.
findings.evidence: secret.mjs:507-508 `A reveal is still heard by the GM that ran it alone (forgetHeldMask): a second GM keeps the name cut, the side that hides.`; mask-gm.mjs:305 calls forgetHeldMask on this GM only.
findings.failure_scenario: Two GMs, both on while Chie is masked; Chie reveals herself. p2, away, returns: askForWords asks both GMs and the first answer wins - if gm2's lands first p2 reads '?'. If gm2 later settles or rewrites that card, every reader's copy goes back to '?'.
findings.refutation_tried: Looked for a hook or store that tells other GMs of a reveal (grep forgetHeldMask: one caller). Not run with two GMs.

verifier.why: forgetHeldMask has one caller, on the GM that runs endMask with 'reveal' (mask-gm.mjs:305); nothing tells another GM's store, and the maskStore drop another GM may observe carries no reason, so it could not tell a reveal from a time-of-day end anyway. It errs on the hiding side and the code says so (secret.mjs:484-485, :507-508), and it is not widened by 1.2.121 (a second GM on while the mask stood already took maskedNow at remember since 1.2.119; keepHeldMask only adds rows). It stays minor rather than nit because the release notes and handbook read 'until the killer reveals themselves' without the exception, and a second GM's updateSecret pushes '?' back onto every reader's copy of a card they already read named.

findings.title: A third whose Escape Together fails is sent the full crisis card, threshold and all, in a masked incident or a trap - the hidden killer's Leg is read off it
findings.what_happens: announceCrisis decides who gets the hidden copy with defenseHiddenFor, which builds the seat's copy with castFor at the moment the card is written and merges it over the GM's own state: { ...state, ...world, ...copy }. A seat that is no longer seated gets {} (or the offer alone) from castFor, so killerId stays the GM's and crisisDefenseHidden answers false. Escape Together's failure runs thirdLeaves (thirdId null) before the card, while the third is still a recipient through also: [actor]. The third is therefore sent the GMs' line 'total < threshold', where threshold includes the hidden killer's Leg. The comment says the copy is 'read at the fight's stage', but only crisisDefenseHidden's input is forced to stage incident; castFor reads the current seats.
findings.evidence: murder-rules.mjs:1943-1945 'if (key === "sharedEscape") { await thirdLeaves(actor);' (failure branch, before announceCrisis at :1959); :2822-2826 thirdLeaves writes thirdId: null; :4387 'incidentAudienceIds(state, { stage, also: [actor] })'; :4415-4416 'const copy = castFor(userId, readCast(), world); return crisisDefenseHidden(key, { ...state, ...world, ...copy, active: true, stage: "incident" });'; incident-store.mjs:579 returns {} or { betrayal } for a user not seated; settings.mjs:3689-3700 incidentSeats seats the third only through cast.thirdId; config.mjs:4192-4194 sharedEscape side third, defense killer leg
findings.failure_scenario: A Direct Murder opens on Hope, so the killer is behind a '?' (Leg +1). Aiko walks in as the third. Her tile says 'Beat 15 + a hidden defense'; she tries Escape Together and rolls 15. The victim's copy of the card says '15 against 15 + a hidden defense: a miss', but Aiko's card says '15 < 16 · with Hope': she reads that the hidden killer's Leg is +1, against D-A9 ('no value'). The same in a trap with a third against the absent builder's Leg.
findings.refutation_tried: Checked whether the third is still a recipient (yes, also: [actor] at :4387); whether castFor would still null killerId for them (no: incident-store.mjs:579 returns before the mask/trap nulling at :588-590 because the third is no longer in incidentAudienceIds(seen)); whether the merge order could drop the GM's killerId (no: copy {} has no killerId key, so state.killerId survives). The trap's own 'shown' number is still computed right. The only rolled killer-defended row that unseats its own taker before the card is Escape Together's failure; Survive and Escape Together's success end the incident and are not affected the same way (not driven).

verifier.why: The road is real and could not be overturned: after Escape Together fails, thirdLeaves has written thirdId null before the card, the third is still a recipient through also: [actor], castFor sends them {} (they are no seat any more), so defenseHiddenFor merges the GMs' state with killerId intact and the third gets the full 'total < threshold' line. Narrower than written in two ways. (1) DEFENSE.cap is 1, so what leaks is one bit - whether the hidden killer's Leg is +1 or better - not a value beyond that; it does break D-A9's 'no value', and it also tells a 0 defence, which no hidden copy ever tells. (2) The failure_scenario's own roll (15 against 'Beat 15 + a hidden defense', a miss) is the case the code and AUDIT item 712 already accept as told by the outcome; the card adds information only when the third's total is below the number shown (e.g. 12: '12 < 16' or '12 < 15'), which is most failures. Survive's and Escape Together's successes are not affected: the stage moves to resolution but the victim and the third stay seated (settings.mjs:3698) and a trap's copy stays indirect, a mask is not ended by finishIncident (endMask callers: mask-gm.mjs:330/338/345, murder-rules.mjs:822, season-wipe.mjs:793). The release notes' line 43 ('their result card says hit or miss without the GM's number') and the player handbook's sentence are untrue for this seat. No test drives a third: tier 2 '1.2.121 CASE-16' is a trap's victim's Self-Defense (passed, base/r121-tier2.log:81). Severity minor: needs a third, Escape Together, a failure and a mask or trap; one bit of a killer's statistic is a clue, not the answer.

findings.title: The watches' dice kept for the lights stay held if endEclipse throws before its last try block, and the next opening on any victim reads them instead of the running watch
findings.what_happens: holdForTheLights sets the module-level lightsDice at eclipse.mjs:424; releaseTheLights runs only in the finally of the try around judgePendingMurders (eclipse.mjs:545-560). advanceTimeOfDay (:491), setClock (:517) and the announces between them sit outside any try, so a throw there leaves lightsDice set until the next endEclipse or a reload. findings.title: A redraw under a typing GM fires the replaced field's change and blur in Chromium, so a window that saves on change or blur commits the half-typed text at every redraw: the GM's Remnant card writes the words being typed to the trace and its copies on every token move
findings.where: scripts/live.mjs:228 (element.replaceWith(next) with the focus in a field of the region; whileEditing on by default, :126); scripts/remnant-ring.mjs:258-259 (the card watches every token, whileEditing: true), :361-370 (blur saves the field); scripts/sfx.mjs:846-849 (the path box adds a file on change), :876-877; scripts/sound-panel.mjs:468
findings.what_happens: With whileEditing (now every region), a watched event while the GM types rebuilds the region at once. Chromium 153 fires change (if the value moved since focus), blur and focusout on the focused old field during replaceWith, while it is still connected, so listeners on the field and delegated listeners on the window both hear them. The Remnant card's three text fields save on blur (setRemnantPublic, then markRemnantEdited; setRemnantPublic sends the changed fields to the copies, remnants.mjs:1452-1456), and the card watches tokens: true, so every token create, update or delete anywhere saves the words typed so far and redraws again; the save's own token write wakes another redraw, which saves again. The Effects path box (sfx:<key>) adds its value as a file on change, so a redraw while a path is half typed adds the half path as a file of the row, and the full path is added beside it when the GM leaves the box. The planner's node fields do the same through its write on change (pre-existing since 1.2.120, whose dashboard already had whileEditing). The text, caret and focus are kept on the new field, as claimed; what is new is the write of the old one.
findings.evidence: Measured, /tmp/r121-R/blur/t.mjs: a focused input typed in and replaced: [change:INPUT:conn:oldXY, blur:INPUT:conn:oldXY, doc-focusout:INPUT:true, focusout]; textarea the same; a select: blur and focusout only. /tmp/r121-R/vR/drive.mjs, 1eee4d62's live.mjs, a GM typing ' ab', a token update, 'cd', a token update: card (blur save as remnant-ring.mjs:361) 4 writes 'Old words ab','Old words ab','Old words abcd','Old words abcd' and world words changed mid-typing; planner field 2 writes; on 03ee8de9's live.mjs (the card's region without whileEditing there) 1 write each, at the end. With 1eee4d62's live.mjs and whileEditing: false: 1 write. Code: live.mjs:126 `whileEditing = true`; remnant-ring.mjs:258 `watch: { items: true, tokens: true, stores: [remnantStore] }`; :361 `field.addEventListener("blur", async () => {`; sfx.mjs:846-848 `input?.addEventListener("change", () => { ... write(soundValueOf(withSoundFile(ownSoundsFor(key), input.value)));`.
findings.failure_scenario: Daily Life: the GM opens a trace's card and rewrites its words for the players while the students walk the map. Each step a player takes saves the GM's words as far as they have typed, and a student who holds that Truth Bullet sees its text change to the half sentence, again and again, until the GM leaves the field. In the Sound window, the GM types a path into an effect's box as another GM edits another effect: the row now draws from two files, the half path that plays nothing and the full one.
findings.refutation_tried: Checked that the old node's listeners are not removed before the swap (wireCardEditing wires the new card in `after`; the old field keeps its blur listener) and that Chromium fires the events with the node still connected (measured). Checked whether live.mjs swallows them: its onChange only acts under a press and onFocusOut only with pending set (live.mjs:294-299, :349-352). Checked jsdom: replaceWith fires nothing, so R7974 and the Room setup and card tests cannot see it. Not measured in Firefox (whose removal is believed to fire no blur) or in Foundry's app; the card's propagation to players' copies is read in source, not run. Confidence 'read' for the module's windows: the mechanism is measured on the module's live.mjs with wiring modelled on the cited lines.

verifier.why: Regression for the Remnant card and the Effects path box (and any other region that was whileEditing false on 03ee8de9 and saves on change or blur); not for the planner, whose region already rebuilt under a named field on 03ee8de9 (measured: old live.mjs with whileEditing true writes the half value too).

findings.title: The Mastermind window's pick, its Hope box's presence and Apply's comparison stay as at the open: the window does not follow another GM's change of the Mastermind beyond the Hope line
findings.what_happens: openMastermindDialog reads `current` once (:619), marks it selected in the `who` select (:622, :655-658) and draws the Give Hope fieldset only if a Mastermind was named at the open (:668). The only live region is `.drpg-mm-live` (:713), the Hope box; it now hears mastermindStore (:721) and Give reads mastermindActor() at the press (:541). The select outside it is never redrawn, a window opened with no Mastermind never grows the box, and Apply compares the form with the open's `current` (:734, applyMastermindChoice :568-594).
findings.evidence: `const current = mastermindActor();` (:619); `
findings.failure_scenario: Two GMs. GM A opens the Mastermind window with nobody named: no Give Hope box. GM B names Ben. A's window still says 'nobody' and has no box; A, unaware, picks Aiko and presses Apply: setMastermind(Aiko) replaces B's pick without A ever seeing it. Or A opened with Aiko named: B names Ben; A's Hope line shows Ben's Hope under a select that says Aiko; A changes only the lair and presses Apply: who (Aiko) equals the open's current (Aiko), so setMastermindLair moves Ben's lair from a window that names Aiko.
findings.refutation_tried: Looked for another keepLive or keepFresh on the window (none: the one region is .drpg-mm-live) and for a re-read of the store in the Apply callback (it returns the form's who and lair only). The notes (v1.2.121.md:55) claim the window follows the change; the code covers the Hope line and Give. ROUTING's 1.2.122 table holds 'r120-F-6's rest' for claude/items-122 without saying what it is; this may be that rest, now with a file:line. Severity minor: two GMs changing the Mastermind while one window stands open is a particular situation, though it is the owner's window rule.

verifier.why: The code reading holds: current is read once (mastermind.mjs:619), the who select and the Give Hope fieldset are drawn at the open (:622, :668-672), the one live region is .drpg-mm-live (:713), and Apply compares with the open's current (:734, :568-594); both failure scenarios follow (a pick over another GM's, or a lair moved under a select naming the old Mastermind). Not new: it is the remainder of r120-F-6 the audit already recorded ('current is still read once at the window's open', ROUTING.md:99) and routed as 'r120-F-6's rest' to claude/items-122 (ROUTING.md:115). What is new in 1.2.121 is the release notes' overclaim (v1.2.121.md:55 'The Mastermind window follows another GM's change of the Mastermind'); the tier-2 test of that name reads only the Hope line and Give (base/r121-tier2.log:140, ok). findings.title: When the bound's end throws in its drops, the frozen mix stays drawn over the new fog, and the next dissolve fades from it
findings.what_happens: At the bound queueBehindDissolve runs done; done shows the incoming sprite first, then drops the other fog sprites (:2305-2307) and the mix (:2308). A throw in a drop (the kind R8030 A plants) skips the rest: released in finally, but the mix - the dissolve frozen at its last tick, t = 0 in a hidden tab, so the old picture - stays renderable above the new sprite, and the outgoing sprite stays resident. A room just found stays covered until the next change, whose dissolve takes the last fog child, the mix, as its 'previous' (swapInFog :2389) and fades from the old picture. Errors logged ('a dissolve let go at its bound could not end itself').
findings.evidence: Sim case 7 on 1eee4d62: after the bound with dropSprite throwing, [fog-S0:off, fog-S1:R, mix:R] busy=false; still so after the late end. 03ee8de9 in the same order: no fog sprite drawn at all.

findings.refutation_tried: Not a regression and not an exposure: it over-covers, and 1.2.120 uncovered everything in the same order. Dropping the mix first, or each drop in its own try, would close it; recorded as a nit.
